Ladies and gentlemen, good day, and welcome to Tech Mahindra Limited Q2 FY27 Earnings 
Conference Call. We have with us today Mr. Mohit Joshi, Managing Director and Chief 
Executive Officer; Mr. Rohit Anand, Chief Financial Officer; and Mr. Atul Soneja, Chief 
Operating Officer.  
As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only mode, and there will be an 
opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need assistance 
during the conference call, please signal an operator by pressing star, then zero on your touch-
tone phone. Please note that this conference is being recorded. 
 
I now hand the conference over to Mr. Mohit Joshi for his opening remarks. Thank you, and 
over to you, sir. 
Mohit Joshi: 
Thank you, and thank you all for joining us, and welcome to our Q2 FY27 earnings call. I just 
wanted to begin by highlighting a significant milestone in Tech Mahindra's journey as we 
celebrate our 40th anniversary this quarter, a very proud moment for associates, customers, 
shareholders, and partners.  
Over four decades, we have built deep client relationships, developed expertise across industries, 
and adapted through successive waves of technology change. From our roots in 
telecommunications, we have grown into a global technology company offering AI-powered 
technology consulting and digital solutions to global enterprises across industries. 
 
Through all this change, the entrepreneurial spirit that shaped Tech Mahindra has endured. It 
drives us to pursue new opportunities, build for the long term, and keep learning at our heart. 
We believe that technology must create meaningful value for our clients and communities. 
Today, that spirit finds its clearest expression in our promise to help clients scale at speed. As 
we mark this milestone, I'm also pleased to announce that our Board of Directors has 
recommended a bonus share issue in a ratio of 1:1 for our shareholders. 
 
Turning to our quarterly performance, we delivered a very strong quarter with broad-based 
growth across the business. Revenues were US$1.693 billion, representing 6.8% year-on-year 
growth on a reported basis and 7.2% growth in constant currency. Positive momentum across 
our verticals and the ramp-up of large deals supported this performance, and we are now winning 
share based on our talent investment and their focus. We have above-industry-tenured staff 
focused on delivering business outcome-oriented solutions to our clients. Operating margins for 
the quarter stood at 14.8%. 
 
From a vertical perspective, in Communications, revenues grew 9.5% year-on-year, supported 
by the ramp-up of the Orange large deal and new strategic engagements. We continue to see 
opportunities across AI-led operational transformation, fiber and network modernization, and 
B2B platform modernization. We also believe the next wave of cost transformation will be 
driven more by technology-led transformation beyond merely AI benefits and labor arbitrage, 
which plays to Tech Mahindra's strengths and deep telecom expertise. 
 
In this quarter, we launched Zero-Gravity Telco Architecture, our North Star framework, 
enabling telecom operators to reduce enterprise gravity by addressing the architectural

payments and wealth management, modernizing client platforms, and strengthening our 
insurance capabilities. During the quarter, we were recognized as a global leader in the ISG 
Guidewire Services Ecosystem 2026 study for the first time, reflecting the progress we have 
made in insurance. 
 
Manufacturing grew 7% year-on-year. Aerospace saw good traction, supported by engineering 
demand and industrial opportunities centered on AI-led efficiency, supply chain visibility, and 
system consolidation. Hi-Tech grew 6.7% year-on-year, supported by new deal wins. AI-led 
product engineering and platform modernization are driving demand. At the same time, cost 
optimization and consolidation initiatives continue to support a healthy pipeline. 
 
Retail, Travel and Logistics grew 9.2% year-on-year, supported by new client wins and the 
ramp-up of consolidation and transformation engagements in the Americas. We continue to see 
opportunities to expand our share within existing accounts and help clients strengthen the 
infrastructure, data, and platforms needed for AI adoption. 
 
Healthcare grew 6.2% year-on-year. Our focus remains on expanding our presence across 
providers and life sciences, with vendor consolidation and AI-led transformation as key areas of 
opportunity. We are building on our AI solutions portfolio and ecosystem partnerships to support 
clients in areas such as post-market surveillance and regulatory compliance. 
Coming to the progress we made under TechM Helix, our AI initiative, this quarter, we 
strengthened the platforms, partnerships, and industry capabilities that underpin all of our AI 
offerings. Our Helix investments are translating into strategic engagements across industries and 
geographies, with many moving beyond pilots towards larger-scale implementation within core 
business processes. 
During the quarter, we secured AI engagements across professional services, healthcare, 
insurance, communications, consumer health, and technology. Let me share examples to 
illustrate how clients are approaching AI as part of broader business transformation. A European 
professional services firm, for instance, selected us to embed AI and agentic AI across more than 
40 customer-facing platforms and products and modernize software engineering, displacing a 
longstanding incumbent. 
Secondly, a US healthcare technology leader engaged us to deploy a multi-agent AI solution 
across its post-market surveillance complaints lifecycle, accelerating triage while preserving 
traceability, regulatory governance, and expert oversight. And thirdly, an APAC communication 
and media provider selected us to transform customer experience operations, embedding AI 
agents across voice and digital interactions, agent assistance, quality, and knowledge 
management.
